summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn shared a vulnerable message titled "I almost quit," reminding the church that what people see on the outside, the fruit and the victories, does not always reveal the fight and pressure happening on the inside. Drawing on about thirty years of ministry, he spoke honestly about seasons of exhaustion, criticism, and discouragement when he wondered whether he could keep going. He stressed that there is a difference between wanting to quit and actually quitting. His encouragement was clear: do not put a period where God placed a comma, because if God is not finished, we do not get to quit.

The message centered on the life of Elijah. In 1 Kings 18, Elijah witnessed a great victory as fire fell from heaven and the people declared that the Lord is God. Yet one chapter later, a threat left him afraid, worn out, and ready to give up, telling God he had had enough. Pastor Travis noted that valleys often follow victories, and that God meets us in our fatigue and fear as faithfully as He meets us in our faith. Alongside 2 Corinthians 4:8-9 and 16, the church was reminded that we may be pressed but not crushed, and that we do not lose heart.

Several lessons followed. Exhaustion can make us question what God has already settled, and God answered Elijah with rest and food rather than rebuke. Pastor Travis taught that tired is a condition while finished is a conclusion, that rest is not retreat, and that we should never make permanent decisions in temporary exhaustion. Isolation, he said, makes quitting sound reasonable, because pain speaks in absolutes and distorts our perspective. Elijah felt like the only one left, yet God showed him seven thousand others, which points to our need for community and church family. God then met Elijah in the cave with a simple question and a gentle whisper, showing that silence does not mean absence and that the cave is a location, not an identity.

Finally, Pastor Travis encouraged listeners to consider that what they almost quit may be connected to what is coming next. Elijah's next assignment included Elisha, someone he had not yet met, and our perseverance may be tied to the breakthrough of others. Closing with Isaiah 40:31, he prayed for renewed strength, hope, and faith, invited weary listeners to receive prayer, and offered anyone the opportunity to surrender their life to Jesus. The church was encouraged to keep going, stay connected, and remember that they are not walking through any season alone.
mainPoints: Valleys and exhaustion often follow victories, but tired is not the same as finished: rest is not retreat, and we should never make permanent decisions in temporary exhaustion.
Isolation makes quitting sound reasonable and distorts our perspective, but God meets us in our caves, speaks in a gentle whisper, and calls us to get connected to community and come back out.
What you almost quit may be connected to what God has coming next, and those who hope in the Lord will have their strength renewed.

versesMentioned.text: We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed.
Therefore we do not lose heart. Outwardly we are wasting away, yet inwardly we are being renewed day by day.

Then the fire of the Lord fell and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the soil, and also licked up the water in the trench. When all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and cried, "The Lord, he is God! The Lord, he is God!"
Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,

while he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness. He came to a broom bush, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. "I have had enough, Lord," he said. "Take my life; I am no better than my ancestors."
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.
And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?

He replied, "I have been very zealous for the Lord God Almighty. The Israelites have rejected your covenant, torn down your altars, and put your prophets to death with the sword. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me."
Yet I reserve seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed down to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.
There he went into a cave and spent the night. And the word of the Lord came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

The Lord said, "Go out and stand on the mountain in the presence of the Lord, for the Lord is about to pass by." Then a great and powerful wind tore the mountains apart and shattered the rocks before the Lord, but the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake came a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire came a gentle whisper.
So Elijah went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, and he himself was driving the twelfth pair. Elijah went up to him and threw his cloak around him.
but those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.

Monday.scripture: Psalm 23:2-3 (NIV): "He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul."
Monday.focus: Rest is not retreat. Sometimes we do not need to quit, we need to recover.
Monday.action: Set a realistic bedtime tonight and plan one simple, nourishing meal. Choose one task you can set aside this week so your body and mind can rest.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank You that You lead me to rest and restore my soul. Help me receive the rest I need and trust You with what I cannot carry today. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 4:16 (NIV): "Therefore we do not lose heart. Outwardly we are wasting away, yet inwardly we are being renewed day by day."
Tuesday.focus: Tired is a condition, not a conclusion. Do not make permanent decisions in temporary exhaustion.
Tuesday.action: Write down one thing you have felt like quitting. Then write one reason you believe God is not finished with it. Wait until you are rested before making any big decision about it.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, when I feel worn down, remind me that You are renewing me day by day. Keep me from giving up on what You have called me to. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 1 Kings 19:18 (NIV): "Yet I reserve seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed down to Baal."
Wednesday.focus: Isolation makes quitting sound reasonable. God wants us connected to community.
Wednesday.action: Reach out today to a trusted friend, family member, or church friend by call or message. Share honestly how you are doing and ask them to pray with you.
Wednesday.prayer: God, show me that I am not alone. Give me the courage to reach out and the wisdom to surround myself with people who point me back to You. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 1 Kings 19:12 (NIV): "And after the fire came a gentle whisper."
Thursday.focus: Silence does not mean absence. Draw closer so you can hear God's whisper.
Thursday.action: Spend ten quiet minutes with your phone put away. Read a short passage, sit still, and write down anything you sense God saying.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, I do not need You to shout. Help me draw near and listen for Your gentle voice. Thank You that You are closer than I think. Amen.

Friday.scripture: 1 Kings 19:19 (NIV): "So Elijah went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat."
Friday.focus: What you almost quit may be connected to what is coming next, and to someone who needs you to keep going.
Friday.action: Send an encouraging message to someone who may be struggling, or share this sermon with them. Remind them: do not quit, keep going.
Friday.prayer: Father, use my perseverance to bless others. Open my eyes to the people You have placed in my path, and help me keep going for their sake and mine. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Isaiah 40:31 (NIV): "but those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint."
Saturday.focus: Hope in the Lord renews our strength, and every cave can become the beginning of a comeback.
Saturday.action: Review your sermon notes and read Isaiah 40:31 out loud. Write a short testimony that begins with "I almost quit, but God," and plan to attend church this Sunday with expectation.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, I place my hope in You. Renew my strength, my faith, and my vision. Thank You that the same God who sustained Elijah sustains me today. Amen.

title: Feeling Like Giving Up? Don’t Quit Yet | I Almost Quit
